nodes.label: Klemens von Metternich
nodes.summary: Austrian foreign minister and central figure at the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Alexander I
nodes.summary: Tsar of Russia who sought expanded influence at the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Karl vom Stein
nodes.summary: Prussian statesman who participated in early Congress discussions but died before its conclusion.

nodes.label: Congress of Vienna
nodes.summary: Diplomatic conference held in 1814 to reorganize Europe after the Napoleonic Wars.

nodes.label: Austria
nodes.summary: Major European power and host nation of the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Prussia
nodes.summary: German state that participated in the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Russia
nodes.summary: Major European power represented at the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Great Britain
nodes.summary: Major European power represented at the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Napoleonic Wars
nodes.summary: Series of wars fought between France and various European coalitions that preceded the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Concert of Europe
nodes.summary: System of balance-of-power diplomacy established after the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Treaty of Paris
nodes.summary: Peace treaty signed on May 30, 1814, preceding the Congress of Vienna.

nodes.label: Nationalism
nodes.summary: Political ideology championed by liberal movements and opposed by Metternich.

edges.evidence_quote: Prince Klemens von Metternich played a central role in the negotiations.
Tsar Alexander I of Russia sought to expand Russian influence.
Baron Karl vom Stein participated in early discussions but died before the Congress concluded.
The resulting Concert of Europe established a balance of power
championing conservatism against nationalist and liberal movements
